extracted.intended_audience: investigative journalists, newsroom editors, journalism students and program coordinators entering the IRE Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for submitting investigative reporting to the annual IRE Awards, including category/size definitions, eligibility, required materials, student-disclosure rules, and judging standards. Covers platform-specific submission limits (print/online, audio, video, longform, books) and special-category rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Investigative Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reporting, through one’s own initiative and work product, of matters of importance to readers, viewers or listeners. In many cases, the subjects of the reporting wish the matters under scrutiny to remain undisclosed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This IRE definition underpins judging. Entries should demonstrate initiative, original reporting and revelation of matters of public importance that may have been concealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging Criterion — Reporter Initiative and Effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantially the product of the reporter’s own initiative and effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges evaluate how much of the work derives from the entrant's independent reporting and effort rather than being driven or produced by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging Criterion — Uncovering Hidden Facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncovers facts that someone or some agency may have tried to keep from public scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should demonstrate discovery of information that was not obvious or intended for public disclosure; showing how facts were obtained strengthens this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging Criterion — Public Importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Be about issues of public importance to the readers, viewers or listeners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should address matters that affect the public interest or civic life, not merely private disputes or solely entertainment-oriented subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging Criterion — Enterprise and Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows enterprise and excellence in documentation, data, storytelling, production, online presentation, and reader or viewer involvement where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation includes quality of documentation, use of data and records, narrative craft, production values (audio/video), online presentation and audience engagement techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Publication/Airing Window
rubrics_metrics.description: All work must have been published or aired between Jan. 1 and Dec. 31 of the award year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 2025 awards, eligible work must have been published or aired between Jan. 1 and Dec. 31, 2025. Entrants should verify publication dates to ensure eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / Previously Published Findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries that include significant investigative findings that were previously published or aired during a prior year are subject to unfavorable judging unless accompanied by a detailed explanation of which findings are new and why it was necessary to include previous work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incorporating earlier findings, provide a clear account of new contributions and rationale for including prior material to avoid penalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification Grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges may disqualify any entry with an incomplete questionnaire. Failure to disclose known challenges to the accuracy or fairness of an entry may result in disqualification or other penalties. Entries disregarding the rules, such as including ads in video or audio will be subject to disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the required questionnaire, fully disclose accuracy/fairness issues, and strictly follow platform rules (e.g., ad removal) to avoid disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest — Judges, Committee and Board Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that included any significant role by an IRE contest judge may not be entered in the contest. Contest Committee members are not eligible to enter or win. IRE Board members who do not serve on either the Executive Committee or the Contest Committee are allowed to enter. Members of the Executive Committee, including the Board Chair, are not allowed to enter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a potential conflict arises, the committee member must discuss with the chair and recuse if warranted; unresolved issues are referred to the Executive Director. Outlets may enter work that includes editing/oversight by committee members provided the committee member did not contribute in a byline-worthy role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be a current member to enter the IRE Awards. At least one journalist named in the story's or series' byline must be a member. For the 2025 IRE Awards, membership must be current through June 30, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries with no current members listed will be disqualified. Entrants must enter the member’s expiration date (day, month, year) when submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category and Size Definitions (Print/Online, Video, Audio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories are organized by platform and size: Print/Online (International, National, Regional, State, Local); Video (International, National, Large Market, Medium Market, Small Market); Audio (Large: National and Regional; Small: State and Local). Size definitions use circulation thresholds and DMA rankings; for partnerships enter the largest organization involved; online-only outlets use primary coverage area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the correct category and market-size based on circulation/DMA rules; miscategorization may affect fees and eligibility. Entry fees vary by category and size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Work Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Original investigative reports completed by students (individual, small team, large team). The reporting, data analysis, interviews and writing must be the work of the students. Professors/faculty may serve in instructional, editing, fact-checking or mentoring roles but may not contribute reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If published by a professional outlet, the professional outlet must have contributed no reporting and the editorial process must be transparently described in a mandatory disclosure statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Disclosure for Student Entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must submit a statement describing how the work was conceived, reported, edited, and (if applicable) published or aired—including any contributions made by others for production or distribution purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe educational context, student ownership of reporting, any stylistic/technical adjustments for publication, and detail any professional contributions involved. This disclosure is mandatory for all student categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary vs Supplemental Materials — Print/Online
rubrics_metrics.description: One story in a series is considered one piece of primary material. You are limited to five primary stories/elements. You may include one additional link and/or PDF as supplemental material. Each file upload has a maximum file size of 3MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For series with more than five stories, select the best five. Supplemental material may include audio/video used elsewhere, follow-up stories, editorials, or elements outside the category limit. Provide login credentials or text versions when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary vs Supplemental Materials — Audio and Video
rubrics_metrics.description: The first 30 minutes of your video or audio file will be considered your primary material. For a series or project that contains multiple pieces, the best 30 minutes can either be compiled into one piece or you can share up to five pieces total (not exceeding 30 mins total). A transcript of your primary stories should also be included. You may include one additional link and/or PDF as supplemental material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer reports should be condensed or entered in the Longform category. Each file upload has a maximum file size of 3MB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript Requirement for Audio/Video
rubrics_metrics.description: A transcript of your primary stories should be included and saved as a PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate transcripts for judges' review. Transcripts are required for audio and video primary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercials/Underwriting/Ads Removal Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercials and underwriting credits must be removed from video and audio entries. This includes bumps and teasers that are not original editorial content or show opens that mention funders or advertising. Any ads left in will result in disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all non-editorial sponsor or advertising content is removed from primary audio/video materials prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and Translation Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries in languages other than English are accepted but must be accompanied by a translation of the story(ies) submitted. Video entries in a language other than English should include a translated script.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide translations or translated scripts so judges can fully evaluate non-English entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry Materials and Checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Required items vary by platform but generally include: current IRE member status and membership expiration date, filled contest questionnaire saved as a PDF, primary materials (links or text/PDF copies), transcripts for audio/video, and any required disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the platform-specific checklist (Print/Online, Video, Audio, Students, Books, Special Categories) before starting the application; cover letter and supplemental materials are optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: File Upload Limits and Formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Each file upload has a maximum file size of 3MB. For books, only eBooks are accepted and entrants must have a link or PDF ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare documents to meet size and format constraints; PDF is the expected format for questionnaires and transcripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry Fees, Refunds and Membership Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees vary from $40 to $100 per entry based on organization size and category. Entry fees do not include an IRE membership. Membership fees range from $25 to $75 depending on career status. Student members can enter for free. All fees are non-refundable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm appropriate fee for category/size and that membership is current; budget for non-refundable fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Category — Tom Renner Award
rubrics_metrics.description: For the best investigative reporting, whether a single story or a lifetime body of work, in print/online, video, audio or book form, covering organized crime or other criminal acts. Limited to 10 stories. Comes with an IRE Medal and $500.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to platform-specific rules for required entry material and adhere to the 10-story limit where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Category — IRE FOI Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors an individual or organization whose significant actions further open records or open government. Comes with an IRE Medal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit documentation of actions that further open records/open government; follow platform rules for required entry materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Category — Investigations Triggered by Breaking News
rubrics_metrics.description: For outstanding investigative work done within 30 days of a news event or development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This award honors deep and quick digging that produces exclusive and timely information; follow platform-specific material requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Category — IRE Award for Sports Investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors investigations that dig into the darker side of sports from amateur leagues to professional organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow platform-specific submission rules; highlight investigative techniques used to reveal systemic or hidden problems in sports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Category — Longform Audio and Video
rubrics_metrics.description: Longform Journalism in Audio and Longform Journalism in Video: For outstanding investigative work primarily presented in audio or video that consists of more than 30 minutes of work. There is no time limit or limit on the number of pieces that can be submitted per project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Longform categories for projects exceeding platform primary limits (30 mins). There is flexibility on length and number of pieces for longform entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Books Submission Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For outstanding investigative reporting that resulted in a published book. Only eBooks are accepted for submission; entrants must have a link or a PDF ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare an eBook link or PDF and the contest questionnaire saved as a PDF per submission checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging Process and Committee Discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Each IRE Awards category is reviewed by screeners. The screened entries move forward to the IRE Awards Committee, made up of members of the IRE Board and other elected and appointed investigative journalists. The Awards Committee determines the finalists, winners, and medalists. At the judges’ discretion, the decision may be made to give no award or award multiple entries in a given category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the multi-stage review process and that final awards are at committee discretion; there may be no winner or multiple winners per category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Entries Allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit to the number of entries you can submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants may submit multiple entries across categories, but must meet membership and material requirements for each entry.
